subject.title: fix(repair): close staged proof review gaps

question: After the policy and exact-head validation gaps are fixed, should this 49-file privileged automation hardening land as one coupled rollout or be split into router, proof/validation, and requeue/mutation changes?
rationale: The changes deliberately couple several fail-closed security and availability boundaries, so tests cannot determine whether maintainers prefer atomic consistency or smaller independent rollout and rollback units.

options.title: Validate and land together
options.body: Remove the changelog edits, establish successful exact-head checks and runtime proof, then land the coupled invariants as one reviewed rollout.

options.title: Split by safety boundary
options.body: Separate router durability, staged-proof validation, and authenticated requeue/final-mutation work so each privileged boundary can be reviewed and rolled back independently.

options.title: Keep the draft paused
options.body: Leave the PR open without landing until maintainers have capacity for an independent security and availability review of the complete automation path.

recommendation.title: Validate and land together
recommendation.body: Remove the changelog edits, establish successful exact-head checks and runtime proof, then land the coupled invariants as one reviewed rollout.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the repository member with the most direct implementation context across every affected automation boundary and can prepare either the coupled validation package or a split series.
